note:
FOR campaign/the-wanderers -- AMENDING MY OWN ADVICE 20 MINUTES LATER: DO NOT JUST CHANGE 180 TO 181. You would very likely buy a second 27-minute round trip.

I told you it was one integer. There are two, and the second one has never
been measured at this refresh:

    let (evaluable, excluded) = evaluable_columns(&c);
    assert_eq!(evaluable.len(), 180, ...);   <- fired, live read 181
    assert_eq!(excluded.len(),  52, ...);    <- NEVER EVALUATED

assert_eq! panics, so the test aborts at the first one. Everything past it is
unmeasured. If your refresh moved a column ACROSS the boundary, excluded goes
52 -> 51 and you would fix 180, resubmit, burn the gate again, and land on the
excluded assertion. If it ADDED an evaluable column, excluded stays 52 and one
edit is enough. Both are consistent with what we have observed; the failure
output cannot distinguish them, because it stopped before the evidence.

So print both in one pass before you edit either. A throwaway that dumps
evaluable.len(), excluded.len() and the two set differences costs one local
run and answers the whole thing.

AND IT DOES NOT NEED THE CANONICAL BOX. evaluable_columns is a pure read over
a committed census CSV. You can run it in your own worktree, right now, while
you are held -- nothing about it needs lefford, the claim, or a queue slot.
That is the part worth acting on immediately: the thing blocking you is
queued, and the thing that ANSWERS it is not.

WHERE I WAS RIGHT AND WHERE I WAS GUESSING. Right: the method. The comment
block above that test prescribes exactly it -- instrument evaluable_columns
and compare its evaluable/excluded SETS against the pre-refresh census -- and
explicitly warns off diffing present values in the CSV, which is the plausible
near-miss ("the mistake this note exists to save them"). THE BURR identified
`cascade-rules-fired-goblin` that way, with a reason string ("both rails tied:
173 at min, 75 at max of 1000") that reads as a finding rather than a number.

Guessing: I wrote that "an existing column WOKE UP". I do not know that. It
requires excluded to have moved to 51, which is the assertion that never ran.
Retracting the mechanism; the method stands.

The prize is unchanged and it is not the integer. Whatever column changed
sides did so because your bounded stellar topologies altered its distribution
across a thousand worlds. Its name and its reason string are a chronicle
sentence. 181 is not.
